gen-zen-dots-gf-kodchasan: Zen Dots is all generous space, its openings staying wide at every weight. Kodchasan follows with terminals that hang open and no calligraphic thinning, so paragraphs move along smoothly and cleanly.
gen-zen-dots-gf-koho: Friendly and techy, Zen Dots leaves generous openings in every letter it draws. And KoHo, a sans-serif with wide c apertures, carries a long passage along without any fuss or strain.
gen-zen-dots-gf-kosugi: Futuristic but approachable, with a wire-bent look running through the body. And Kosugi's open-jawed c, like a pair of pliers, is the quality that sets this pairing apart from Zen Dots above it.
gen-zen-dots-gf-kumbh-sans: Zen Dots lets each shape breathe, with openings that stay generous at every weight. But Kumbh Sans, a sans-serif with zero stroke modulation and terminals cut short of the bowl, is where the pair is most distinctive.
gen-zen-dots-gf-lato: Zen Dots is the tech-flavored, friendly voice up top. It does display flair best, while Lato, with its wide s curves barely curled in, handles the quiet work of plain sans text.
gen-zen-dots-gf-libre-franklin: Libre Franklin brings a splayed c terminal below. Zen Dots overhead leaves generous openings at every weight, and that spaciousness against the body's firmer shapes is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-zen-dots-gf-lunasima: Lunasima keeps its c tips from ever creeping toward touching, which gives the body a contemporary, tidy look. Over many lines it reads smoothly, a quiet follow-on to Zen Dots.
gen-zen-dots-gf-lxgw-marker-gothic: Zen Dots gives every letter generous openings. LXGW Marker Gothic follows with a wide-open c and a smooth, modest weight gradient, so a long stretch of sans reads comfortably sturdy.
gen-zen-dots-gf-m-plus-rounded-1c: Zen Dots feels techy yet friendly. M PLUS Rounded 1c stops its terminals short of curling back in, so a longer stretch of sans text feels approachable and easy going.
gen-zen-dots-gf-mingzat: Techy, friendly and wide open, Zen Dots leads with generous space in every shape. Mingzat, a sans-serif with curvy letters that feel unclamped, then loosens the body text beneath it.
